draft.title: Consequences of river decline
card: When river flows are low, water moves slowly and less fresh water arrives. Salt in the water and soil becomes more concentrated, so salinity can rise.
Warm, slow, nutrient-rich water can let blue-green algae multiply. Some blooms make toxins that can harm animals and people, and can make water unsafe to drink or use.
Low flows can also cut oxygen in the water and shrink the places where fish live, so fish kills may follow. Wetlands that depend on river water can dry out.
These changes can harm wildlife, farms that need clean water, towns that rely on the river and First Nations communities, whose culture and Country are linked to the rivers.
draft.remember: Low flows can bring salinity, algae, fish kills and drying wetlands, and these affect both nature and people.

a.q: Which change in a river is a direct result of low flows letting warm, slow water build up nutrients?
opts: Salt may be washed out of the soil
Fish may find more places to live
a.why: Warm, slow, nutrient-rich water can let blue-green algae multiply, and some blooms are toxic. The other options describe more water or healthier habitat, which are the opposite of what low flows bring.
a.clue: Think about what grows in warm water that barely moves.

b.q: During a long dry spell, the river near the town of Wirrin, a made-up town, runs low and slow. Dead fish appear and the council warns residents not to use the water. Which explanation fits best?
opts: Low oxygen and a toxic algal bloom in the slow water
Too much floodwater washing fish out of the river
Wetlands filling up and pushing fish onto the banks
Fresh water arriving faster and cooling the river
b.why: Low flows can cut oxygen and let toxic blue-green algae grow, which can cause fish kills and make water unsafe to use. The other options describe more water or faster flow, but this river is running low and slow.
b.clue: Ask whether this river has more water or less.

b.best: Low oxygen and a toxic algal bloom in the slow water
